title: Common Thorn Apple (Rwiziringa) in Banana Plantations

Header: Common Thorn Apple (Rwiziringa) in Banana Plantations
Datura stramonium Rwiziringa (Kinyarwanda); Stramoine commune (French); Common thorn apple (English)

Prevention: Use mulching to suppress the weed
Monitoring: Look for erect herb up to 2 m tall, often much-branched, dark green leaves with irregular margins, trumpet- shaped white flowers, fruits are yellowish to brown with spines, and seeds are dark brown to black
Check for the presence of the weed before flowering and consider management to prevent seed set and spread
Direct Control: Hand removal or hoeing before seed set gives sufficient control in small plots
Shake off soil, spread to allow plants to dry out and decompose
Restrictions: Herbicide use is not advisable for smallscale farming as practised in
Rwanda, as it is not cost effective and environmentally friendly
Application of chemical herbicides would pose risk of poisoning as banana leaves are used for cooking and as fodder.
